title: US yield shock, oil surge hammer equities; Nifty hits lowest since April 7 - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
The growing global uncertainty and a sharp spike in US bond yields triggered a broad-based sell-off in equity markets, dragging BSE Sensex to their lowest levels in three months.

The BSE Sensex tumbled 1,248 points to close at 73,581, while the Nifty 50 shed 384 points to end at 23,063 on Thursday. The Nifty 50 slipped to its lowest level in 118 trading sessions, touching levels last seen on April 7. While the Sensex fell to a 76-session low, revisiting levels seen on June 11.

Selling pressure was widespread, with all major Nifty sectoral indices ending in the red. The broader Nifty Smallcap 100 and Nifty Midcap 100 indices declined 1.53 per cent and 2.08 per cent, respectively.

The rupee remained under pressure, weakening by 22 paise to close at 95.96 against the US dollar, as geopolitical tensions fuelled a sharp rise in crude oil prices and pushed US Treasury yields and the greenback higher.

According to Vaibhav Chugh, Chief Executive Officer of Abakkus Mutual Fund, the sharp decline in domestic equities was driven by US 10-year Treasury yields reaching their highest level in nearly two decades, coupled with hawkish commentary from Federal Reserve officials signalling the possibility of further rate hikes.

The yield on the US 10-year Treasury climbed above 5.10 per cent, a level last seen in 2007, while Brent crude prices surged past the $102-$106 per barrel range.

“In the short term, foreign institutional investor (FII) flows could remain sensitive to rising US yields, which offer relatively higher risk-free returns,” Chugh said said.

Back home, a consultation paper issued by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) proposing tighter caps on distribution payouts also triggered sharp selling in select stocks.

“Although valuations in India have moderated from their long-term averages, they have not yet become attractive enough to trigger a strong return of foreign investors. Corporate earnings have remained resilient, and if that trend continues over the next few quarters, FIIs are likely to gain the confidence needed to increase allocations to India,” Chugh added..
